Restate only the main (public) question.
Compute \(19 \times 44 + 17 \times 29\).

First, calculate \(19 \times 44\):
\[19 \times 44 = 19 \times (40 + 4) = 19 \times 40 + 19 \times 4 = 760 + 76 = 836.\]

Next, calculate \(17 \times 29\):
\[17 \times 29 = 17 \times (30 - 1) = 17 \times 30 - 17 \times 1 = 510 - 17 = 493.\]

Now, add the results:
\[836 + 493 = 1329.\]

To verify the main result, let's try another approach:
Calculate \(17 \times 29\) again but using a different method:
\[17 \times 29 = 17 \times (30 - 1) = 17 \times 30 - 17 = 510 - 17 = 493.\]
And \(19 \times 44\) can also be checked:
\[19 \times 44 = 19 \times (40 + 4) = 19 \times 40 + 19 \times 4 = 760 + 76 = 836.\]
Adding these gives:
\[836 + 493 = 1329.\]

The answer to the main question is confirmed to be 1329.
